title: Etale locality of the base-change map
statement:
Consider a base-change square
and let $\{U_i\to X\}$ be an etale covering such that $U_i\to S$ factors
as $U_i\to V_i\to S$ with $V_i\to S$ etale; form the associated
Cartesian diagrams

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
U_i & \xleftarrow{h_i} & U_i\times_XY\\
f_i\big\downarrow & & \big\downarrow e_i\\
V_i & \xleftarrow{g_i} & V_i\times_ST,
\end{array}
$$

and put $\mathcal F_i=\mathcal F|_{V_i\times_ST}$ and
$K_i=K|_{V_i\times_ST}$ for a sheaf $\mathcal F$ resp. a complex $K$
on $T_{\Et}$.

1. If $f_i^{-1}g_{i,*}\mathcal F_i=h_{i,*}e_i^{-1}\mathcal F_i$ for
all $i$, then $f^{-1}g_*\mathcal F=h_*e^{-1}\mathcal F$.
1. If $f_i^{-1}Rg_{i,*}K_i=Rh_{i,*}e_i^{-1}K_i$ for all $i$, then
$f^{-1}Rg_*K=Rh_*e^{-1}K$.
1. If $\mathcal F$ is an abelian sheaf and
$f_i^{-1}R^qg_{i,*}\mathcal F_i=R^qh_{i,*}e_i^{-1}\mathcal F_i$
for all $i$, then
$f^{-1}R^qg_*\mathcal F=R^qh_*e^{-1}\mathcal F$.

(*Stacks Project, Lemma [Tag `0EZR`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EZR).*)

proof.text: Write $a_i:U_i\to X$, $b_i:V_i\to S$, $c_i:T_i=V_i\times_ST\to T$, and $d_i:Y_i=U_i\times_XY\to Y$. The last two are etale by base change [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-continuous]. The fiber-product universal property identifies $Y_i$ with $U_i\times_{V_i}T_i$: a compatible pair is precisely a pair $(u,t)$ with $f(a_i(u))=g(t)$ and the forced $V_i$ coordinate $f_i(u)$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Use [lem-weil-pbc-etale-site-localization-open] for $V_i,U_i,T_i,Y_i$ to identify their small etale sites with the corresponding slice sites. Its explicit equivalence of sites also identifies set-valued sheaves: the covering equalizer condition is unchanged under that equivalence [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets].

For a sheaf $G$ on $S_{\Et}$, inverse-image composition and $fa_i=b_if_i$ give $a_i^{-1}f^{-1}G\cong f_i^{-1}b_i^{-1}G$ [lem-weil-pbc-site-morphism-composition]; the two etale inverse images are restriction [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-restriction], [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction]. Similarly $ed_i=c_ie_i$ gives $(e^{-1}F)|_{Y_i}\cong e_i^{-1}F_i$. Apply the direct-image comparison in [lem-weil-pbc-slice-site-localization] to $g$ at $V_i$ and to $h$ at $U_i$: $(g_*F)|_{V_i}\cong g_{i,*}F_i$ and $(h_*E)|_{U_i}\cong h_{i,*}(E|_{Y_i})$. In the abelian case these are also the explicit comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-underived-exchange-restriction](1). Substituting gives $(f^{-1}g_*F)|_{U_i}\cong f_i^{-1}g_{i,*}F_i$ and $(h_*e^{-1}F)|_{U_i}\cong h_{i,*}e_i^{-1}F_i$. Neither calculation requires $U_i=X\times_SV_i$.

Restriction to any of these slices is exact [lem-weil-pbc-site-restriction-exact] and preserves arbitrary K-injective complexes [lem-pur-kinjective-restrict-localized], applied to the constant ring $\mathbf Z$. Abelian sheaves carry their unique $\mathbf Z$-module structure (multiplication by an integer is repeated addition); this identifies abelian sheaves with modules over the constant integer sheaf. Thus the cited ringed-site assertion applies to the unbounded complexes here. Exactness identifies termwise restriction with its derived functor [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization].

source.place: Tag 08FI, label lemma-restrict-K-injective-to-open; discussion preceding it

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-slice-localization] to $g:T\to S$ at $V_i$ and to $h:Y\to X$ at $U_i$, with constant integer coefficients. The continuous base-change functors are supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-continuous], and constant coefficients and the inverse-image functors agree with the abelian ones by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] at $R=\mathbf Z$. This yields $(Rg_*K)|_{V_i}\cong Rg_{i,*}K_i$ and $(Rh_*E)|_{U_i}\cong Rh_{i,*}(E|_{Y_i})$, natural in arbitrary unbounded $K,E$ and compatible with derived adjunctions. Inverse images are exact [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact], so the inverse-image comparisons in step 2 apply termwise and descend by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. With $E=e^{-1}K$, the two restricted global terms are therefore $f_i^{-1}Rg_{i,*}K_i$ and $Rh_{i,*}e_i^{-1}K_i$.

Use [lem-sbc-base-change-arrow-localization] with $U=U_i$, $B=V_i$ and $f_U=f_i$. Its hypotheses are exactly that $a_i,b_i$ are etale and $fa_i=b_if_i$; its localized $Y_U$ is the $Y_i$ of step 1. Its equation $C_R\circ r_U(\beta_F)=\beta_{U,F_B}\circ C_L$ identifies the restriction of the global underived arrow with the local arrow under the comparisons in step 2, for both sets and abelian groups.

Use [lem-sbc-derived-base-change-arrow-localization] with the same $U_i,V_i,f_i$ and arbitrary $K$. Its equation $C_R^D\circ r_U(\beta_K)=\beta_{U,K_B}\circ C_L^D$ identifies the restricted global derived arrow with the local arrow under step 4's comparisons. Its cohomology clause identifies their maps in every integer degree. In particular the statement applies to $F[0]$ in the single degree $q$.

For clause (1), let $A=f^{-1}g_*F$ and $B=h_*e^{-1}F$. Steps 2 and 5 identify $\beta_F|_{U_i}$ with an isomorphism by hypothesis. For each object $W\to X$ the base changes $W_i=W\times_XU_i\to W$ form a covering [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-continuous]. Given $s\in B(W)$, take its unique inverse image in $A(W_i)$ on each $W_i$. On $W_i\times_WW_j$ those inverse images agree, because their images agree and the locally restricted map is injective. The sheaf equalizer condition [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets] glues them uniquely to a section of $A(W)$ mapping to $s$. Two sections of $A(W)$ with the same image have identical restrictions to all $W_i$ and hence are equal by the same sheaf condition. Thus every component of $\beta_F$ is bijective; the inverses commute with restrictions by uniqueness, so $\beta_F$ is an isomorphism. This argument includes the empty covering of the empty scheme (the empty equalizer forces singleton section sets).

source.place: Tag 0EZR, label lemma-base-change-local, last sentence of proof of (1)

proof.text: For clause (2), steps 4 and 6 show that the restriction of $\beta_K$ is an isomorphism on every $U_i$. Exact restriction [lem-weil-pbc-site-restriction-exact] commutes with cohomology: apply it to the kernel, image and quotient defining $H^r$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] to get $(H^r\beta_K)|_{U_i}=H^r(\beta_K|_{U_i})$. For each fixed integer $r$ the latter is an isomorphism. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-cover-detects-iso] the abelian sheaf map $H^r\beta_K$ is an isomorphism on $X$. Since this holds for every $r\in\mathbf Z$, [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology] shows that $\beta_K$ is an isomorphism in $D(X_{\Et})$. No truncation or uniform cohomological bound is used.

source.place: Tag 0EZR, label lemma-base-change-local, proof of (2), using cohomology sheaves after Tag 0D6G

proof.text: For clause (3), put the abelian sheaf $F$ in degree zero. By definition $R^qv_*F=H^q(Rv_*F)$, and the degree-$q$ base-change map is $H^q(\beta_F)$ (with the exact inverse-image identifications); this is the degreewise convention in [sbc-def-base-change-map] and [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Exact restriction commutes with kernels, images and their quotients as in step 8, so taking $H^q$ in the comparison of steps 4 and 6 identifies the restriction of the global degree-$q$ map with the local degree-$q$ map. The hypothesis gives an isomorphism on every $U_i$ in this one degree. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-cover-detects-iso] to that abelian sheaf map to conclude. This does not assume the hypotheses of clause (2) or any comparison in other degrees. The argument applies to every integer $q$ without needing a separate vanishing assertion.

blueprint_update.statement:
Consider a base-change square
and let $\{U_i\to X\}$ be an etale covering such that $U_i\to S$ factors
as $U_i\to V_i\to S$ with $V_i\to S$ etale; form the associated
Cartesian diagrams

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
U_i & \xleftarrow{h_i} & U_i\times_XY\\
f_i\big\downarrow & & \big\downarrow e_i\\
V_i & \xleftarrow{g_i} & V_i\times_ST,
\end{array}
$$

and put $\mathcal F_i=\mathcal F|_{V_i\times_ST}$ and
$K_i=K|_{V_i\times_ST}$ for a sheaf $\mathcal F$ resp. a complex $K$
on $T_{\Et}$.

1. If $f_i^{-1}g_{i,*}\mathcal F_i=h_{i,*}e_i^{-1}\mathcal F_i$ for
all $i$, then $f^{-1}g_*\mathcal F=h_*e^{-1}\mathcal F$.
1. If $f_i^{-1}Rg_{i,*}K_i=Rh_{i,*}e_i^{-1}K_i$ for all $i$, then
$f^{-1}Rg_*K=Rh_*e^{-1}K$.
1. If $\mathcal F$ is an abelian sheaf and
$f_i^{-1}R^qg_{i,*}\mathcal F_i=R^qh_{i,*}e_i^{-1}\mathcal F_i$
for all $i$, then
$f^{-1}R^qg_*\mathcal F=R^qh_*e^{-1}\mathcal F$.

proof.text:
Restricting to $U_i$ and using the factorizations
$U_i\to V_i\to S$ gives

$$
(f^{-1}g_*\mathcal F)|_{U_i}=f_i^{-1}(g_*\mathcal F|_{V_i})
=f_i^{-1}g_{i,*}\mathcal F_i,
$$

where the first equality is the compatibility of inverse and direct
images with localization of the etale site of
[def-weil-pbc-etale-site] (Sites, Lemma 7.28.2,
[Tag `03EF`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03EF)) and the second uses
$\mathcal F|_{V_i}=\mathcal F_i$, and likewise

$$
(h_*e^{-1}\mathcal F)|_{U_i}=h_{i,*}e_i^{-1}\mathcal F_i.
$$

Since $\{U_i\to X\}$ is an etale covering, a morphism of etale sheaves
whose restrictions to all $U_i$ are isomorphisms is an isomorphism
([def-weil-pbc-etale-site]), which proves (1); the assertions (2)
and (3) are the same argument with the localization compatibility for
the higher direct images and sheafified cohomology
(Cohomology on Sites, Lemma 21.20.4, [Tag `0D6G`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0D6G)), applied
degreewise for the $R^q$'s of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] and to
$R^q$ of the base-change maps of [sbc-def-base-change-map].
